I am 65 years old. I finished primary school. I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. My family has 7 people, and some of my sons work off-farm in the city, so we have a little cash coming in, but I still count every yuan. I learned everything I know by doing it and watching the men who farm around me.

I divide my land like this: 5 mu I rotate wheat and maize on, and 4 mu I plant cotton.

For wheat, I already sowed it last October, but I am managing it now. Before sowing, I ran the rotary tiller twice to break up the soil. I put 30 jin of improved wheat seed per mu. For fertilizer, I spread one bag — 100 jin — of 18-18-9 compound fertilizer when I sowed. Then at green-up time in March, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 40 jin. I irrigate 4 times total: once in winter if the weather is dry, and three more times in spring, using my well. I spray pesticide 3 times — twice for insects, once for weeds. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, and I expect about the same this year if we do not get a late frost.

For maize, I plant it right after wheat harvest in early June. I buy hybrid seed, the kind like Denghai or Nongda, 1 package per mu, about 2.5 kg. I do not till the soil for maize — I plant directly into the wheat stubble to save time and fuel. I put 80 jin of 28-6-6 compound fertilizer in the row at sowing. When the plants are knee-high, I topdress with 30 jin of urea. I irrigate twice — once right after sowing if it does not rain within a week, and once when the tassels come out. I spray 3 times for insects and weeds. If the summer rain comes at the right time, I get 950 jin per mu.

Cotton is on the other 4 mu. I rotary till in April and sow 3 jin of improved cotton seed per mu. Cotton needs a lot of food, so I put 100 jin of 26-10-15 compound fertilizer at sowing. When it starts flowering in July, I spread another 80 jin of 15-15-15 compound. I irrigate 3 times. But cotton is a headache for pests — I spray 12 times from June to August, sometimes every 10 days, for bollworm and aphids. The spray costs money, but if I skip even one, the bolls drop and the crop is finished. I expect about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I do what I did last year because it worked. I watch my neighbors. If Old Wang puts more fertilizer on his wheat, I put more on mine. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family.
